title: Expanded circle equation: complete the square
subtitle: Circles · 14 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **14 of the official questions in Circles are this one** — 0 Easy, 1 Medium, 13 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The equation looks like x² + y² + ax + by + c = 0, with no brackets.
- Or the question says a circle has some center and radius and its equation is x² + y² + Dx + Ey + F = 0, and asks for one of the constants.
- Harder versions add a second circle with the same center and double the radius or diameter.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Group the x terms and the y terms.
- Add (half the x-coefficient)² and (half the y-coefficient)² to both sides.
- 2) Rewrite as (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r² and read off the center and radius.
- 3) For a second circle, keep the center, scale r (doubling r multiplies r² by 4), then expand back out or substitute a given point if the question asks for a constant.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Graph the expanded equation as given, because Desmos handles implicit equations, and read the center and radius from the picture.
If there is an unknown constant, make it a slider and adjust it until the circle passes through the given point or has the required size.
Do this as a check next to the algebra, because values that aren't whole numbers are hard to read off a graph.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You forget to add the completing-the-square constants to the right-hand side as well.
Or, when the radius doubles, you double r² instead of multiplying it by 4.
Or, when you expand back out, you drop the constant term that the new center creates.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
